question: Point \(P\) lies on the bisector of \(\angle AOB\). Its distance to \(OA\) is \(3\). What is its distance to \(OB\)?
solution: A point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the two sides of the angle, so the distance from \(P\) to \(OB\) is also \(3\).

edges.reason: Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.
Distances to the angle sides are perpendicular segment lengths, so point-to-line distance is part of the property itself.
